security_problem: A terminal allow for tools/call must not be relayed unless its final allow record has been durably committed to the trusted audit sink opened by Visor. Trusted set: the Visor binary and policy, the configured audit directory and its filesystem namespace for the process lifetime, and audit file ownership/host administration. Untrusted: the MCP client, agent, MCP server, tool names, arguments, and results. Pathname namespace mutation (hostile host users, root, operator deletion, concurrent rename/unlink/rebind of the audit path or an audit-directory ancestor, pathname reachability after startup, rotation, reopen, or following a moved inode) is outside the model: the deployment violates the H19-v2 trust boundary if the audit directory is mutable by an attacker, and this boundary is declared rather than compensated with more filesystem code. Ancestor walks, SameFile, link-count checks, runtime path revalidation, O_EXCL state machines, and namespace-race defense are explicitly rejected.
required_behavior: The logger opens the audit file once with os.O_RDWR|os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW and mode 0600, rejects anything not a regular file via f.Stat(), and recovers prevHash/chainIndex from that same opened *os.File using ReadAt (no pathname reopen recovery). NewLogger performs an unconditional one-time parent-directory fsync whether the ledger is new or existing, and never unlinks or cleans up the pathname on failure. Every terminal allow (approved allow, explicit allow, and default/fallback allow) builds the final audit.Event with all existing redaction, identity, receipt, and policy evidence, calls CommitAuthorization which appends the complete newline-terminated hash-linked record, requires a full write (io.ErrShortWrite on short write), explicitly calls file Sync, and only then advances prevHash/chainIndex; any marshal/write/short-write/sync/closed/poison/non-durable failure poisons the logger and converts the call to deny before either transport can relay it. The proxy increments denied and returns execution denied without mutating taints, allowed/approved metrics, or chain state on failure. Log(Event) returns error and advances chain state only after a full append. MustLogger keeps stderr/fallback behavior but marks those sinks non-durable so authorization commit always fails closed.
failure_behavior: Marshal failure, write error, short write, file sync failure, closed sink, poisoned sink, stderr/fallback sink, non-regular sink, and incomplete/corrupt restart tip all deny the tools/call with zero relay and no allowed-state mutation (no taint marking, no allowed/approved metric increment, no in-memory hash-chain advancement). Failed commits poison the logger so later Log and CommitAuthorization calls return ErrAuditSinkUnhealthy without another write.
